newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, platinum down.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals end mixed, platinum down.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended mixed on Friday, with most of platinum futures extending early losses due to a further slip in spot platinum while gold and palladium ending mostly up, traders said.
Activity was moderate as the currency market was calm after its volatile moves on Thursday.
Gold futures ranged from one yen per gram lower to five yen up. Benchmark April gold was up four yen at 1,246 yen.
With the exception of July platinum, which was up 25 yen, platinum futures ranged from seven to 41 yen down. Benchmark April was off seven yen at 1,361 yen.

Trading in gold futures was directionless amid uncertainty over near-term trends in the currency market, while spot gold is likely to probe the downside support at $340 per ounce with no bullish factors in sight, the traders said.
Spot gold was quoted a tad weaker at $341.00/341.50 per ounce at 0721 GMT, against $341.30/80 in New York on Thursday.

For platinum group metals (PGM), spot platinum is likely to tread weaker in a technical correction after the recent extreme volatility, while the acute shortage in physical supplies after the protracted Russian sales suspension will support palladium, traders said.

"Although Russia's platinum group metals agency said it would resume PGM sales in the spot market in late June and contract sales in July, TOCOM palladium would be supported by short-covering," one trader said.
"Any price dip would be an opportunity for investors to cover their shorts," he said.
Palladium futures ranged from 14 yen per gram lower to seven yen up. Benchmark April was flat at 563 yen.
Benchmark silver was up 0.7 yen per 10 grams at 174.7 yen.
